results.term_definition:
Luminosity is the energy output per second from some emitting body such as a star. The most common use is for electromagnetic radiation, in which case the range of wavelengths or frequencies needs to be specified. The radiative energy per second at a specific frequency or wavelength is called "luminosity density". The luminosity across all electromagnetic wavelengths is referred to as "bolometric luminosity".

Other forms of luminosity include neutrino emission or material outflows such as jets. 

In astronomical contexts, luminosities are often expressed as multiples of the Sun's luminosity, known as solar luminosities.
